item.description:
The right panel is complete: History keeps every version of an artifact and shows what changed, Devices moves out of Settings with Forget… for a Mac you no longer use, and Suggestions lists the artifacts most like the one you're reading. A shelf on this Mac can move into iCloud Drive at any time.
### What's new
- The right panel gains History, on ⌥⌘3: every version of an artifact's content Sediment has seen, newest first under the day it was kept, with Current and Read marked. A click on a version shows what changed since the one before it, paragraph by paragraph, in place of the page. Return from the list opens the newest version's changes, J and K walk to older and newer versions, and Escape brings the page back. Versions live in the shelf folder and are thinned as they age, so a shelf shared between Macs shows the same history on each. It takes the place of the Highlights placeholder. - The right panel gains Devices, on ⌥⌘1: every device that opens your shelf, grouped as Not caught up, Up to date and Retired, each saying when it last opened the shelf and how many deletions wait on it. Retire and Restore sit beside each device, as they did in Settings, and a device with nothing waiting can be retired too. It takes the place of the Comments placeholder, and Settings no longer has a Macs section. - Activity's line about a device that hasn't opened the shelf in a while now says to retire it under Devices (⌥⌘1). - A retired device can be forgotten 30 days after it last opened the shelf: Forget… asks first, then takes it off the list on every Mac. If it opens the shelf again, it rejoins as a new device. - The right panel gains Suggestions, on ⌥⌘4: up to eight artifacts whose names and tags most resemble the selected one, best first, each with the date it last changed and the tags it shares. A click opens that artifact, and Back (⌘[) returns. Archived artifacts are included and the Trash is not. It takes the place of the Links placeholder, and the panel's tabs now read Devices, Tags, History, Suggestions, on ⌥⌘1 to ⌥⌘4 in that order, so Tags moves to ⌥⌘2. - Return from the list walks the suggestions: it opens the first, J and K step through the list as it stood when you pressed Return, and Escape goes back to the artifact you started from. - Settings ▸ Shelf folder shows where your shelf lives — iCloud Drive, the built-in folder or a folder you choose — with a way to each. Keep in iCloud Drive…, also in the File menu, copies your shelf into the Sediment folder in iCloud Drive and leaves the folder it was in unchanged. If that folder already holds a shelf, Sediment shows that one instead and adds nothing to it.
### Fixed
- A copy iCloud Drive makes of a file whose contents match the artifact already on the shelf is set aside instead of appearing as a second artifact. - A notice about many files names three of them and counts the rest, instead of listing every one. - The launch banner's line about files still arriving goes away once a pass finds nothing left to wait for.

A fresh install can keep its shelf in iCloud Drive and share it across your Macs, a right panel lists the shelf's tags beside the artifact, and Activity, Dismiss Notices and Share move to the function row.
### What's new
- On a fresh install Sediment asks once whether to keep your shelf in iCloud Drive. Return keeps it there, in a Sediment folder iCloud Drive shows at its top level, and a second Mac signed in to the same account opens the same shelf on its first launch. Escape keeps it on this Mac, as before. An existing shelf is left exactly where it is and is never asked. - When iCloud Drive cannot be reached, or the signed-in account changes, the shelf says so in a banner rather than quietly moving. The badge beside the Sediment wordmark reads iCloud, and Settings spells the folder the way Finder does. - A right panel opens beside the artifact on ⌥⌘1 to ⌥⌘4, closed in every new window. Its Tags tab lists every tag on the shelf with its count, the selected artifact's tags tinted; a click opens that tag's collection, and a click on the collection you are in returns to the Shelf. Highlights, Comments and Links are placeholders for now. - Activity, Dismiss Notices and Share are F1, F2 and F3. Each used to sit one modifier away from a frequent chord on the same key and was pressed by mistake. The old ⌥⌘0, ⌥⌘N and ⇧⌘C do nothing, and the shortcuts sheet says to hold fn with the three. - A double-click on a sidebar row opens the artifact in a new window. - An unread artifact's date is set semibold in the link colour beside its bold name. - A tag that matches what you typed in Go to… is listed first, and ⇥ completes the highlighted tag.
### Fixed
- Return closes the Keyboard Shortcuts sheet; Escape still does. - ⇥ and ⇧⇥ stay in Go to…'s query field instead of leaving it. - Choosing a folder whose files iCloud Drive has not finished delivering is refused with a message to try again shortly, instead of opening an empty shelf. - Running the sediment command before the app has ever opened a window now says to open Sediment and choose where to keep the shelf, instead of deciding for you.

A tag's collection can be saved to the sidebar's footer and opened with a chord, the line under the wordmark states facts while a key legend in the corner shows what you can press, and a first install comes as a disk image.
### What's new
- Save Collection (⌘D) keeps the collection you are in as a row in the sidebar's footer. The first six take ⌘4 to ⌘9 by position, each chord drawn beside its tag. Move Collection Up and Down (⌃⌘↑ and ⌃⌘↓) or a drag reorder them, and ⌘D inside a saved collection removes it. The saved list travels with the shelf to your other Macs. - The line under the Sediment wordmark states facts only: what is unread on the Shelf, and the Trash's size. - A key legend in the bottom-right corner shows the chords that work right now: Restore in the Archive and the Trash, Delete Now in the Trash, and Save or Remove Collection and Show Shelf in a collection. The Shelf stays quiet, and notifications sit higher to clear the legend. - A first install comes as a disk image beside the zip, and the app dragged out of it updates itself from then on.
### Fixed
- A name pasted into the rename field with a line break in it is drawn on one line.
